description: All 81 files in content/lexemes/ are Claude drafts (review: "draft", source: "generated") covering every lexeme used by content/drafts/batch_001.json and batch_002.json. Check lemma, gender, declension/conjugation, gloss and — for the five pronouns — the full irregular paradigm, then approve: `npm run content:approve -- content/lexemes/*.json`. Sentences can't be approved before their lexemes (ADR-010).
reason: ADR-010: draft lexemes make every form built from them `unverified`, and block sentence approval.

description: 40 A1 sentences drafted by Claude (snt_0011–snt_0050), 50 drillable tokens, aimed at noun cases across all six declensions plus common preposition government (uz + acc/gen, no/pie/bez/zem + gen, par + acc, ar + ins). Approve with `npm run content:approve -- content/drafts/batch_002.json` once the lexemes are approved. Try them first in the app with `npm run dev:drafts` (ADR-011).
reason: ADR-007: drafts only ship after human approval.

description: RESOLVED as a draft (2026-09-25, ADR-010): pronouns keep their whole paradigm in the lexeme's `irregular` map, keyed by form key; inflect() never uses ending tables for them. See lex_es, lex_mes, lex_vins, lex_vina, lex_tas — please confirm the approach while reviewing those paradigms.
reason: Surfaced while reviewing content/drafts/batch_001.json for M2 prep; blocks writing correct lexeme entries for any pronoun above.

description: The schema now accepts `mood: "debitive"` as a token feature (added 2026-09-19 to unblock batch_001 snt_0005's "jāstrādā"), but how mood combines with tense (e.g. present debitive "jāstrādā" vs. past debitive "bija jāstrādā") isn't designed yet. Needs a decision before src/engine/inflect.ts handles verbs.
reason: Provisional schema addition, not a verified linguistic model — flagged in docs/SPEC.md and src/content/schemas.ts.

description: All seven files in content/grammar/ (noun_decl1..6.json, alternations.json) are Claude drafts (review: "draft", source: "generated"). Please check each cell, delete any you're unsure of (a gap is fine), then run `npm run content:approve -- content/grammar/<file>.json` per file. The expected paradigms in src/engine/__fixtures__/nouns.ts (5-6 nouns per declension) are the quickest way to review: if a fixture paradigm is right, the table cells it exercises are right.
reason: ADR-008: until approved, inflect() marks every form from these files confidence: "unverified".

description: Singular vocative is a gap in every noun table. Declension 1 has competing forms (draugs! / draug!), personal names often drop the ending (Pēter!, Ann!), and SPEC.md puts the vocative mostly out of scope. Decide: leave as gaps, fill with one canonical ending per declension, or handle only via irregular maps on the few lexemes that need it.

Masculine nouns of declension 4 (puika) and declension 5 (bende, and male surnames in -e like Zīle) need their own tables: at least dat.sg differs (-am / -em instead of -ai / -ei). Until they exist, such lexemes report no-table rather than a wrong form. Please supply the full masculine paradigms.
reason: The existing declension 4/5 tables are gender: "f" on purpose.

description: alternations.json has an identity rule st → st (so valsts → valstu, not valsšu). Confirmed for declension 6; please confirm whether declension 2 (-stis nouns) and declension 5 (-ste nouns, e.g. kaste) also keep st unchanged in their alternation slots, or alternate (st → š?).
reason: Applied to all declensions today because it is a single rule list.

description: No rules exist for f → fj, ll → ļļ, nn → ņņ — stems ending in these are left unchanged. Please confirm whether they alternate and add the rules if so.

Known words that skip or change the regular pattern must carry an `irregular` map on their lexeme once they're authored: declension 2 nouns in -ns/-ss with gen.sg in -s (akmens, ūdens, rudens, mēness, zibens), declension 2 nouns without alternation (tētis → tēta, viesis → viesa), declension 6 nouns without alternation in gen.pl (acs → acu, auss → ausu, zoss → zosu, balss → balsu). This list is a reminder, not complete.
reason: The round-trip check will flag these as mismatches if the irregular map is missing — that's the intended signal.
